'''Menas C. Kafatos''' ({{langx|el|Μηνάς Καφάτος}}; born 25 March 1945) is a Greek-born American physicist and a writer on spirituality and science. His publications include: ''The Nonlocal Universe'' and ''The Conscious Universe''. Kafatos has written and lectured extensively promoting discourse between science, spirituality, and religion. He has held numerous positions at institutions including [[Chapman University]], [[George Mason University]], and [[NASA Goddard Space Flight Center]].

==Career==
Kafatos received his B.A. in physics from [[Cornell University]] in 1967 and a Ph.D. in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1972.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = http://www.chapman.edu/our-faculty/files/curriculum-vita/Kafatos-Menas-CV.pdf|title = Curriculum Vitae|accessdate = 2014-05-30|website = |publisher = |last = Kafatos|first = Menas}}</ref> After postdoctoral work at [[NASA Goddard Space Flight Center]], he joined [[George Mason University]] and was University Professor of Interdisciplinary Sciences from 1984-2008, where he also served as dean of the School of Computational Sciences and director of the Center for Earth Observing and Space Research.<ref name=":0" /> He and a team of computational scientists joined [[Chapman University]] in the fall of 2008, where he was the Founding Dean of the Schmid College of Science and Technology serving as dean from 2009 – 2012.<ref name=":0" /> He currently is the director of the Center of Excellence in Earth Systems Modeling and Observations (CEESMO).

Kafatos has authored books including ''The Conscious Universe'', ''The Non-local Universe'' (with [[Robert Nadeau (science historian)|Robert Nadeau]], [[Springer-Verlag]] and [[Oxford University Press]]), ''Principles of Integrative Science'' (with Mihai Draganescu, [[Romanian Academy of Sciences]] Press), and more than 300 [[Peer-reviewed journal|peer reviewed]] publications, cited by over 750 other articles.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://academic.research.microsoft.com/Author/12520618/menas-kafatos|title = Microsoft Academic Search|accessdate = 2014-05-29|website = Menas Kafatos|publisher = [[Microsoft]]|url-status = dead|archiveurl = https://archive.today/20140529191852/http://academic.research.microsoft.com/Author/12520618/menas-kafatos|archivedate = 2014-05-29}}</ref>

Menas was one of the speakers in [[Bhagavad Gita]] Summit (from 10–1 December 2021) during [[Gita Jayanti]] at [[Dallas]], [[Texas]], US along with other notable personalities such as [[Mukundananda|Swami Mukundananda Ji]], [[Shiv Khera|Mr. Shiv Khera]], [[Kiran Bedi]], [[Gloria Arieira|Brahmacharini Gloria Arieira]], [[Dantu Muralikrishna]] and others.<ref>{{cite web |title=JKYog Bhagavad Gita Summit {{!}} RKTemple |url=https://www.radhakrishnatemple.net/jkyog-bhagavad-gita-summit |website=adhakrishnatemple.net |publisher=[[Radha Krishna Temple]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Renowned speakers from all over world to attend JKYog Bhagavad Gita Summit |url=https://www.business-standard.com/content/press-releases-ani/renowned-speakers-from-all-over-world-to-attend-jkyog-bhagavad-gita-summit-121121000554_1.html |website=www.business-standard.com}}</ref>

===Research===
Kafatos' peer-reviewed research has focused on [[cosmology]], [[astrophysics]], [[natural hazards]], [[climate change]], [[Earth system science]], and [[remote sensing]]. Although he has written books around meta-physical interpretations of quantum phenomena he does not have substantial peer-reviewed work in [[quantum physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=menas+kafatos&hl=en|title = Google Scholar}}</ref>

Notable scientific contributions include enhancements to synthetic [[tropical cyclone]] ([[hurricane]]) circulations used in forecast models,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ma|first=Yimin|author2=Kafatos, Menas |author3=Davidson, Noel E. |title=Surface pressure profiles, vortex structure and initialization for hurricane prediction. Part I: analysis of observed and synthetic structures|journal=Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics|date=July 2012|volume=117|issue=1–2|pages=5–23|doi=10.1007/s00703-012-0190-z|bibcode = 2012MAP...117....5M |s2cid=119388579}}</ref> new perspectives on the self organization of the universe through the lens of [[complexity]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1-link=Neil Theise|last=Theise|first=N.D.|author2=Kafatos, M.|title=Sentience Everywhere: Complexity Theory, Panpsychism & the Role of Sentience in Self-Organization of the Universe|journal=Journal of Consciousness Exploration & Research|date=2013|volume=4|issue=4|pages=378–390|url=http://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/291|accessdate=2014-05-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Theise|first=N.D.|author2=Kafatos, M.|title=Complementarity in biological systems: a complexity view|journal=Complexity|date=2013|volume=18|issue=6|pages=11–20|doi=10.1002/cplx.21453|bibcode=2013Cmplx..18f..11T|doi-access=free}}</ref> a detailed look at the relationship between vegetation in the United States and [[El Niño]]/[[Southern Oscillation]],<ref>{{cite journal|last=Zuotao|first=Li|author2=Kaftatos, Menas|title=Interannual Variability of Vegetation in the United States and Its Relation to El Niño/Southern Oscillation|journal=Remote Sens. Environ.|date=2000|volume=71|issue=3|pages=239–247|doi=10.1016/S0034-4257(99)00034-6|bibcode=2000RSEnv..71..239L|citeseerx=10.1.1.39.6376}}</ref> and a better understanding of [[dust]] and [[aerosols]] over [[India]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Gautam|first=R|author2=Hsu, NC |author3=Lau, K.M. |author4=Kafatos, M |title=Aerosol and rainfall variability over the Indian monsoon region: distributions, trends and coupling|journal=Annales Geophysicae|date=September 2009|volume=27|issue=9|pages=3691–3703|doi=10.5194/angeo-27-3691-2009|bibcode = 2009AnGeo..27.3691G |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=El-Askary|first=Hesham|author2=Gautam, R.|author3=Singh, R.P.|author4=Kafatos, M.|title=Dust storms detection over the Indo-Gangetic basin using multi sensor data|journal=Advances in Space Research|date=2006|volume=37|issue=4|pages=728–733|doi=10.1016/j.asr.2005.03.134|bibcode = 2006AdSpR..37..728E }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kafatos lives in [[Marina Del Rey]], California, with his wife Susan Yang, a scientist in the fields of [[computational biology]], [[experimental biology]], and [[neuroscience]]. They met while working together at [[George Mason University]]. His brother, [[Fotis Kafatos]], was a [[biologist]] and founder and honorary president of the [[European Research Council|European Research Council (ERC)]]. Kafatos has 3 children: Lefteris, Stefanos, and Alexios. He is the chairman of the board for the [[American Hellenic Council]].

==Awards and honors==

===Awards===

* 2011 [[IEEE]] Orange County Chapter Outstanding Leadership and Professional Service Award

===Honors===

* 2013 [[National Observatory of Athens]] Affiliated Researcher
* 2013 [[Kyung Hee University]] International Scholar
